results.evidence: Section 2.2: "On expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive five-year Renewal Terms ... Renewal ends only if either Party gives the other written notice of non-renewal not more than 210 days and not less than 180 days before the end of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term. Pricing for each Renewal Term shall be Kogein's then-current list price ... All other terms of this Agreement, including the Minimum Annual Volume under Section 3.2, continue to apply during each Renewal Term."
results.reason: The problem is present and still actionable for Stabind. The Initial Term ends January 31, 2029, so the 30-day non-renewal window falls around mid-2028 and has not yet opened. Missing it locks Stabind into a five-year renewal at whatever list price Kogein alone sets. The 180,000-lb take-or-pay Minimum Annual Volume would also continue for that renewal. The September 2026 side letter does not touch Section 2.2; it amends only Section 11.2(d). The Chronic Failure reduction of the Minimum Annual Volume is expressly disputed and reserved, so it does not cure the issue. No document gives Stabind a price cap, any other exit right, or a longer notice period. Stabind can still diary the window or negotiate an amendment.

results.evidence: DPA §1.1(b): "'Kogein Group Member' means Kogein; any Affiliate of Kogein; and any entity with which Kogein has a strategic supply or processing arrangement." Supply Agreement §1.3: "'Kogein Group Member' has the meaning given in Section 1.1 of the Data Processing Addendum." Supply Agreement §15.2: "Kogein may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any Kogein Group Member on written notice to Stabind."
results.reason: The Supply Agreement adopts the DPA definition by express cross-reference. That definition reaches well beyond Affiliates (which §1.1(a) limits to control relationships) to any entity with which Kogein has a 'strategic supply or processing arrangement'. That could include a rival brewer. The §17.4 precedence clause does not help Stabind, because the Supply Agreement contains no competing definition. So Kogein can move the whole Agreement, or part of it, to such an entity on notice alone, while Stabind's own assignment needs Kogein's consent. The assignee would take on Stabind's Blend Specifications, Forecasts and ordering history. The §4.2 and §9 restrictions would bind the assignee as successor, but they would not stop a competitor from learning that information. Stabind has no right to object or terminate on such an assignment or on a change of control. The 2026 Side Letter amends only §11.2(d) and does not touch §15.2 or the definition. The Agreement is still running, with an Initial Term to January 2029 and five-year auto-renewals, and no assignment has occurred that Stabind has accepted. The problem is therefore live and actionable, for example by narrowing the definition or adding a consent or termination right.

results.evidence: Section 3.1: "Section 11.2(d) of the Agreement is deleted and replaced in its entirety with the following: '(d) Product Contamination Losses, to the extent arising from Kogein's willful misconduct.'" Section 5.1: "This Side Letter is a signed side letter and an amendment for purposes of Sections 17.3 and 17.4 of the Agreement."
results.reason:
The problem is present and it hurts Stabind.

1. **What the amendment does.** Under the original Section 11.2(d), Product Contamination Losses were uncapped whatever their cause. These are Stabind's own recall costs, destroyed beer and equipment remediation. The Side Letter limits that carve-out to willful misconduct.

2. **The new carve-out adds nothing.** Section 11.2(c) already excludes willful misconduct from the cap, so the new 11.2(d) is redundant.

3. **Negligent contamination is now capped.** Ordinary negligent or no-fault contamination falls under the Section 11.1 cap of 12 months' fees.

4. **The consequential-damages exclusion may now apply.** Section 11.3 excludes such damages except for claims in Section 11.2, so it may now reach recall costs and lost-beer losses.

5. **The indemnity does not fill the gap.** Kogein's indemnity in Section 10.1 covers only third-party claims, not these first-party losses.

6. **The Side Letter governs.** Section 17.4 ranks signed side letters first, and Section 5.1 invokes that ranking.

7. **Nothing in the letter cures it.** Kogein gives no consideration for the change. The letter's operative terms are a reservation of rights, an invoicing standstill and a remediation plan that does not change service levels.

8. **It remains actionable.** The letter was drafted by Kogein and sent for countersignature, and the signature blocks are blank. If it has not been signed, Stabind should refuse or renegotiate Section 3. If it has been signed, Stabind has a live cap exposure for any future contamination event. The exposure is heightened by the Ridgeline Haze launch using Yakima hops. The folder records no contamination event or accepted outcome that would make this history.

results.evidence: Section 4.2 of the Service Level Schedule: "If a Chronic Failure occurs, Stabind may elect one of the following by written notice to Kogein given under Section 16 of the Agreement within thirty (30) days after delivery of the Performance Report for the second of the two consecutive calendar quarters". Side Letter recital 1.2: "On July 8, 2026, Kogein delivered to Stabind its Performance Report for the calendar quarter ended June 30, 2026" and "On August 28, 2026, Stabind delivered to Kogein a written notice (the "Election Notice")".
results.reason: The problem is present and still actionable. Q1 2026 (88%) and Q2 2026 (89%) were both below 92%, so a Chronic Failure occurred. The 30-day election window ran from the July 8, 2026 Performance Report and closed on August 7, 2026. Stabind's Election Notice was delivered on August 28, 2026, which is 21 days late. Nothing in the documents extends or tolls the window. Section 3.3 and Section 5.2 of the Schedule say disputes and escalation do not suspend any time period. Section 4.5 also bars reusing the Q1 and Q2 quarters toward a later Chronic Failure. Kogein has asserted untimeliness, which puts at risk Stabind's 50% Minimum Annual Volume reduction for the 2026 Contract Year and later years, and its exposure to a shortfall invoice. Stabind has not accepted the result. Side Letter Sections 2.1 and 2.2 expressly reserve both parties' positions with no waiver, and Section 2.3 only defers the shortfall invoice. The dispute is therefore live, and the client should address it, for example with waiver or estoppel arguments or a negotiated resolution.
